observation_summary: The test fails because the generated tool-tip fragment contains unescaped double quotes, resulting in an invalid HTML attribute string. The expected output includes escaped quotes ("), while the actual output contains raw quotes.
reasoning_summary: The issue is a failure to correctly escape special characters (double quotes) within a string generation method. This is a procedural logic error in how the tool-tip string is constructed, which is a classic Algorithm/Method defect. It is not a missing guard (Checking), a wrong constant (Assignment), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object).
evidence_used: junit.framework.ComparisonFailure: expected:< title="Series ["A"], 100.0" alt=""> but was:< title="Series ["A"], 100.0" alt="">
evidence_gaps: The actual implementation code of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment was not provided in the snippets, but the failure clearly points to a string manipulation logic error.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not an incorrect initial value, but rather a failure in the procedural logic that processes and escapes the input string.
While one could argue a check for quotes is missing, the primary failure is the incorrect transformation of the string, which is an algorithmic step.
